method: Three actually inspected ordinary front/courtyard/aerial pictures and current standard PMTiles; no bespoke archival or survey research.

references.observed: Actually inspected daylight Piazza Colonna facade: pale warm plaster, five window rows with large grilled lower windows, alternating triangular/curved principal-floor pediments, square mezzanine windows, two upper rows, deep cornices and rusticated corner quoins. A central dark arched entrance has a balcony above. The terracotta pitched roof has short chimneys and a tall roof loggia near the west/north corner. Original geometry will omit heraldry, inscriptions and decorative sculpture.

Actually inspected the internal court: deep open ground-floor arcades on square stone piers, closed rear walls/doorways behind the arcade, pale walls, ornate window frames, a very tall arched stair window, upper rectangular openings, several layered floor cornices and shallow original plaster panels. The court is open to the sky; a photograph crop does not establish all hidden rear elevations.

Actually inspected the oblique aerial photograph. Tricolor illumination identifies the long south-facing principal range around Piazza Colonna; lighting colors must not be copied into the material palette. Connected north/east/west ranges surround the open court, with varied roof levels and rooftop loggia. Montecitorio, the column, nearby square-front palaces and the independent block along Via del Corso remain native context. Roof inventories are partly concealed by night exposure.
